evals.prompt: I want to add a new subcommand to docex called `doctor` that runs a set of local health probes (docker reachable, project.yml present, etc.) and prints a report. Walk me through exactly where the new code goes and how the CLI gets wired up to dispatch `docex doctor` to it. Be specific about file paths, the function names and signatures docex expects, how dispatch actually happens, what else has to be touched for the command to show up correctly, and what the docex development process requires me to keep in sync when I make this change.
evals.expected_output: A correct answer adds a handler function `_cmd_doctor(args: list[str]) -> int` in src/docex/__main__.py that builds its own argparse.ArgumentParser and lazily imports a run_doctor(...) entry point from a new subpackage module (the implementation living under a purpose-named subpackage such as src/docex/pipeline/doctor.py or a sibling, NOT a per-command package and NOT src/docex/doctor/), registers `doctor` in the _build_handler_table() dict (the hand-rolled dispatch mechanism — not argparse subparsers, not click/typer), and adds entries to _HELP_TEXT and the appropriate _GROUPS tuple so it renders in --help. It should also note the docex five-artifact alignment discipline from docex_process.md (doctrine prose first, then plans/core, tables, src, tests) and that tests must be added.
